title: Find the Longest Valid Obstacle Course at Each Position
summary: Given an array of obstacle heights, for each index i, determine the length of the longest obstacle course that includes the i-th obstacle and maintains a non-decreasing order of heights up to that point.
statement: Given an array of obstacle heights, for each index i, determine the length of the longest obstacle course that includes the i-th obstacle and maintains a non-decreasing order of heights up to that point. Return an array where each element represents the length of such a course for the corresponding index.
constraints: obstacles has 1 through 100000 positive heights, each at most 10000000.
For each index, the course must end at that index and choose earlier positions in order.
Course heights must be nondecreasing, so equal heights may extend a course.
hints: This is a longest nondecreasing subsequence ending at every position.
Maintain the smallest possible tail for each course length and use upper-bound search for the current height.
Upper bound permits equality. The tail invariant makes i the longest extendable length, so i+1 is optimal specifically at this position.
editorial: Upper bound permits equality. The tail invariant makes i the longest extendable length, so i+1 is optimal specifically at this position.

tests.explanation: The final height two extends the course [1,2], producing lengths [1,2,3,3].
The second equal height extends to length two, while the final lower height starts a new course.
